domain: Guarded window-tilemap draw: given (x,y,width,height,mode), computes a base cursor into *Data_03001e8c at ((y<<5)+x)*2, bails out unless 2<=width<=30 and 2<=height<=30, then walks the INTERIOR rows/columns only (row 1..height-2, col 1..width-2, i.e. skipping the outer ring) writing 16-bit tile values built from a running tile-index counter masked with 0xFFF and OR'd with a fixed 0x127 flag, choosing between two different column-vs-row stride patterns depending on whether the 5th (stack) argument is zero. Sets base[0xEA3]=1 (a dirty/redraw flag, one past the template's own RENDER_ALT_OFS=0xEA2) on the drawn path.
notes: The generated family report clustered this owner with template-main-0801e260 (clear_tile_attributes_in_rect.c) at 8626 bp -- the highest score of any owner in this assignment batch -- but the reference assembly shares only the coarse (y<<5)+x cursor idiom and the Data_03001e8c base with the template; there is no tile-value masking against 0x3FF, no RENDER_TILE_ATTR_OFS/RENDER_ALT_OFS bit-clear logic, and the real control flow (four-way bounds guard, interior-only double loop with two mode-selected stride shapes) is unrelated to the template's parametrized rectangle clear. The template gave a starting hint about the base-pointer/global (Data_03001e8c, shared with 0801e318 and the template) but essentially no usable control-flow shape.

The exact tile-index arithmetic is genuinely uncertain. There is no `muls` instruction anywhere in the reference, so the per-column tile-index step in the mode==0 branch is produced by repeated addition of a loop-invariant stride register (confirmed from the reference's r0 += r2 pattern inside the inner loop, where r2 is recomputed each outer-row iteration as something derived from height-2) rather than a single multiply -- this candidate's 'tile += stride' loop reflects that repeated-add shape, but the exact base value fed into the running counter (this draft guesses 0xF000-2, i.e. treating it as (0xF000 + row) with a col=0 offset of -2) is not independently confirmed against the reference's literal pool words, which were not individually resolved to their source position without assembling.

Two candidate hypotheses were scored for the tile-index formula in the mode==0 branch: a per-column additive stride (this draft, retained) at 127 differing halfwords / 172 wrong instructions, and a per-column multiplicative-looking 'row + col*width' form at 129/149 (rejected below, since 172 vs 149 wrong_instructions favors the second but differing_halfwords -- the project's primary decision metric -- favors the first, and neither is remotely close to zero). Given how close and inconclusive the two are, and that neither reaches the template's level of match, this genuinely needs the pool words resolved from a real disassembly rather than further guessing.

This is a source-shape gap requiring dedicated reconstruction (correct disassembly of the four literal-pool constants in each pool group, and confirmation of the mode!=0 branch's row-major write pattern against the reference byte-for-byte), not a good target for further family-transplant attempts against the assigned template.

rejected_experiments.experiment: model the mode==0 interior fill as a transposed write where the VRAM cursor itself strides by (height-2) per column (i.e. treat the tile-index computation and the VRAM write address as the same pointer)
rejected_experiments.result: worse (worse structural match, abandoned before scoring) -- the reference clearly keeps two separate values live across the inner loop (r0, the running tile-index accumulator that strides by height-2 each column; and r1, the VRAM cursor that strides by a flat +2 each column), which a single merged pointer cannot reproduce.

rejected_experiments.experiment: model the mode==0 tile-index as tile = 0xF000 + row + col*(height-2) (a per-column additive stride, matching the reference's repeated-add pattern and the absence of any muls instruction)
rejected_experiments.result: best result so far: 127 differing halfwords / 172 wrong instructions at 258/282 bytes. Retained as the candidate.

rejected_experiments.experiment: model the mode!=0 branch's tile-index as tile = 0xF000 + row + col*width (row-major across the full width instead of the additive-stride shape used in mode==0)
rejected_experiments.result: produced 129 differing halfwords / 149 wrong instructions overall (mode==0 branch unchanged) -- fewer wrong_instructions but slightly more differing_halfwords than the retained candidate; inconclusive, not clearly better, and still far from exact, so not adopted as the retained draft.
